title: macp-mcp gate policy (gate.json)
description: Which tool calls on one upstream MCP server need a MACP session, and how that session is run. Rules are tried in order; the first whose tool pattern matches decides. A call that matches no rule is forwarded to the upstream untouched. Loaders also enforce two rules a schema cannot: threshold <= the rule's participant count, and participants never contains the gate's own MACP_AGENT_ID.

server.description: The upstream's configured name. It is the "server" member of the context_id preimage, so changing it changes every context_id.

tool.description: Tool name: an exact name, or a glob where * matches any run of characters (including none) and ? matches exactly one. No other wildcard syntax; matching is case-sensitive and covers the whole name.

mode.description: The MACP mode of the approval session.

participants.description: MACP agent ids of the approvers. The gate itself is the session initiator and never one of them.

threshold.description: APPROVE ballots (Quorum) or votes (Decision) needed to forward the call. Defaults to a strict majority of participants: floor(n/2) + 1. Must not exceed the participant count. With a bound policy that overrides the threshold (for example policy.packs.two-agent-rule), set the same value here.

ttl_ms.description: Session TTL. A session still open after ttl_ms plus a 5000 ms grace is cancelled by the gate and the call refused.

policy_version.description: An RFC-MACP-0012 policy registered with the runtime, bound to the session at SessionStart and evaluated at commitment. The gate must keep commitment authority (initiator_only or any_participant); a designated_role policy such as policy.packs.human-signoff cannot be used. Omitted means the runtime default policy.

description.description: Free text for humans; ignored by the gate.
